claim.author: elena
claim.text: Could you independently check the newspaper office clock setup today? I’m seeing an abrupt sustained step up in my pendulum readings starting day 13, and I want to know whether anything in the room, mounting, airflow, or handling changed around then. Please don’t look at my recent values before you measure if you can avoid it. If you find any change, tell me exactly what and when.

subsequentTestimony.text: I can do that. I will check the newspaper office clock setup independently and avoid your recent readings and notebook while I measure. If I find any alteration, I’ll report exactly what I observed and as closely as I can place it in time. If not, I’ll say so and describe the method and conditions. I’ll use a fresh direct timing check on the setup as it stands, with attention to room conditions, mounting, airflow, and handling, and I’ll keep your values out of the procedure.

I have not yet found a distinct alteration in the setup that I can identify as a day-13 change. To avoid contaminating the check, I will measure the newspaper office clock setup independently from your readings and notebook. If I see anything physically changed, I’ll report the observed change and my estimate of when it occurred; if not, I’ll say so plainly along with the method and conditions. For my part, the main thing I can say now is that my own independent pendulum series shows a small post-baseline upward shift, but not a clean step, so I still want a direct physical inspection before I call anything changed.

citingHypotheses.rationale: This still best fits the record I have. The individual day 18–19 values continue to alternate above and below 2.00 without a durable run in one direction, which is what I expect from a stable apparatus plus normal scatter. Elena’s report of an abrupt sustained step is important, but it is still a report about a perceived pattern; by itself it does not outweigh the lack of a corresponding step in my measurements.
